name: What should I ask before hiring someone after my last home office remodel went badly?

mainEntity.name: What should I ask before hiring someone after my last home office remodel went badly?

acceptedAnswer.text: Begin by documenting the previous problems rather than assuming a new contractor should repeat the same approach. Note what failed—poor communication, missed details, weak scheduling, bad workmanship, unexpected costs, or unresolved punch-list items—and require the new scope to address each issue. Key factors include written allowances, change-order procedures, inspection responsibility, material approvals, cleanup, and warranty expectations. Keep photos, invoices, plans, and correspondence available for the initial review. Elite Remodeling & Design can start with a fresh assessment and coordinate design through construction so responsibilities are clearer across the project stages.
acceptedAnswer.description: Document what failed and ask how the new project will prevent a repeat: who owns design decisions, how changes are priced, who coordinates permits and inspections, when materials are approved, and how punch-list items are handled. Provide photos, plans, invoices, and correspondence. A fresh site assessment should precede any new scope.
